title: Adhesion Frequency Assay for In Situ Kinetics Analysis of Cross-Junctional Molecular Interactions at the Cell-Cell Interface
protocol: Prepare EAS-45 solutions by weighing up all ingredients from Table I.
Dissolve the weighed ingredients in 100-200 ml of DI water.
Add water to make a total volume of 1000 ml solution and adjust pH to 8.0.
Filter and aliquot the solution into 50 ml portions.
Freeze the aliquoted solutions at -20°C for storage.
Draw 3-5 ml of blood from the median cubital vein into a 10 ml tube containing EDTA.
Gently mix the blood with EDTA immediately to avoid clotting.
Transfer the blood to a 50 ml centrifuge tube.
Add 10 ml of cold and sterile Histopaque 1077 to the tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 1000 rpm, 4°C.
Repeat the above steps twice with Histopaque 1077.
Add 10 ml of cold and sterile PBS to the tube after centrifugation with Histopaque.
Centrifuge again for 5 min at 1000 rpm, 4°C.
Remove supernatant from the sample.
Wash RBCs four times in total with cold and sterile PBS by repeating centrifugation steps.
Wash RBCs twice with sterile EAS-45 solution (centrifuging for 5 min @ 1000 rpm, 4°C).
During the last washing step, transfer RBCs to a new sterile 15 ml tube.
Resuspend RBCs in 10 ml of EAS-45.
Remove all supernatant after centrifuging RBCs for 5 min @ 1000 rpm, 4°C.
Put 10 μl of RBC pellet into each of several vials.
Add corresponding amount of PBS to each vial according to Table II.
Make fresh Biotin-X-NHS/DMF 1:10 dilutions.
Add 10 μl of 0.1M borate buffer to each vial.
Calculate the amount of biotin solution needed for each vial and add it immediately.
Vortex each vial after adding the calculated amount of biotin solution.
Place each RBC vial inside a 50ml conical tube.
Incubate on rotator for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Wash each vial three times with 800 μl of EAS-45 for 2 minutes @ 2000rpm.
Add 100 μl of EAS-45 to each vial and store at 4°C.
Prepare a 2mg/ml streptavidin solution according to manufacturer's instructions.
Aliquot the streptavidin solution and store it at -20°C if not used immediately.
Mix an equal amount (10μl) of RBCs from step 2.7 with the streptavidin solution.
Vortex immediately after mixing and incubate on rotator for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Wash three times with 500 μl of EAS-45 for 2 minutes @ 2000rpm.
Add 15μl of EAS-45/1% BSA to each vial and store at appropriate conditions.
Mix an equal amount (10μl) of RBCs from step 3.3 with a 20μg/ml ligand solution.
Vortex immediately after mixing and incubate on rotator for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Wash twice with 500 μl of EAS-45/1% BSA for 2 minutes @ 2000rpm.
Add 15μl of EAS-45/1% BSA to each vial and store at appropriate conditions.
Incubate ligand-coated RBCs with respective mAbs for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Incubate receptor-bearing cells with respective mAbs for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Incubate cells with irrelevant isotype-matched antibodies as controls for 30 minutes at room temperature.
If primary antibodies are not fluorescently labeled, incubate with fluorescently-conjugated secondary antibodies according to manufacturer's instructions.
Analyze samples by flow cytometry using corresponding fluorescent calibration beads.
Pull micropipettes from capillary tubes using PN-30 Narishige Magnetic Glass Microelectrode Horizontal Puller or Sutter Instruments Micropipette Puller.
Adjust the tip of the pulled micropipette to a desired size using micromanipulator and microforge.
Prepare the cell chamber by cutting microscope cover glass to the desired size.
Seal the chamber with mineral oil from both sides to avoid medium evaporation during the experiment.
Add receptor- and ligand-bearing cells to the chamber.
Aspirate interacting cells using respective pipettes.
Use computer-programmed piezoelectric translator to drive RBC in and out of contact with the other cell with controlled contact area and time.
Detect adhesion events by observing RBC elongation upon cell separation.
Repeat the contact-retraction cycle 50-100 times for a given contact time.
Record observed adhesion events by adding "1" for adhesion or "0" for no adhesion in an Excel spreadsheet column.
Use recording devices, such as digital media or videotape, to capture microscopic images.
Record the adhesion frequency versus contact time curve using at least three different cell pairs for each contact time.
Obtain a mean and SEM from recorded data.
Record nonspecific binding curves by using RBCs coated with irrelevant ligands (e.g., BSA) and/or blocking the ligands or receptors using their specific functional blockade mAbs.
Calculate specific adhesion frequency at each contact time point by removing nonspecific adhesion frequency.
Incubate neutrophils with 1 μg/ml of E-selectin-Ig for 10 minutes.
Wash the cells after incubation with E-selectin-Ig.
Incubate the cells with 10 μg/ml of PE-conjugated anti-human CD11a mAb or irrelevant mouse IgG1 as a control.
Wash the cells thoroughly after antibody staining.
Analyze the stained cells immediately using a BD LSR flow cytometer.
Calculate the mean fluorescent intensity (FI) for each peak value from calibration bead histograms.
Plot a linear regression of Log10 PE molecules per bead against Log10 fluorescence.
Pull micropipettes using PN-30 Narishige Magnetic Glass Microelectrode Horizontal Puller.
Cut the pulled micropipettes to desired size opening using a microforge system.
Incubate RBCs with 10 μg/ml of biotinylated goat-anti-human Fc antibody after the streptavidin incubation step.
Add 1 μg/ml of dimeric E-selectin-Ig to the chamber medium to upregulate αLβ2 binding.
Incubate RBCs with human IgG instead of ICAM-1-Ig to control for nonspecific binding in one condition.
Use RBCs not coated with capture antibody as another condition to control for nonspecific binding.
Add 10 μg/ml human IgG to the medium to minimize binding of E-selectin-Ig in solution to the capture antibody on the RBC surface.
